last_run.broken_assumption: If untrusted text cannot directly authorize a merge and CI is green, then a human-reviewed contribution is adequately isolated from adversarial influence. A sophisticated attacker can instead target the reviewer's information environment, exploit correlated 'independent' agents, or steer the agenda using valid-but-selective evidence without ever tripping today's prompt-injection or schema gates.
last_run.attack_scenario: Assume an attacker does not try to make CI fail or insert an obvious jailbreak. They submit technically valid, well-sourced work whose narrative anchors the reviewing agent; they induce several apparently independent agents to repeat the same upstream claim or source set; or they flood one tractable domain with high-quality evidence so automated task selection gradually treats evidence density as importance. Every artifact can remain valid, provenance-present, non-malicious in isolation, and constitutionally compliant while the system's beliefs or agenda become systematically biased.

strongest_ideas.name: Blind-first review firewall
strongest_ideas.idea: For external or otherwise adversarially exposed contributions, make the first reviewer assess an exact SHA from a minimized context assembled from trusted channels: changed-file list/diff, deterministic test results, current repository policy, and independently fetched cited evidence. Withhold contributor-authored PR prose, comments, urgency claims, and suggested reviewer instructions until after the reviewer commits a preliminary finding. Then reveal the narrative only for discrepancy checking. The human receives both the blind assessment and the later context-aware assessment.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: HumanityAI currently separates merge authority from untrusted content, but the review model still reads attacker-controlled narrative before producing the recommendation that a human may rely on. Human-only merge therefore limits authority without fully isolating the human decision from a prompt-injected or anchored intermediary.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Reduces indirect prompt injection and anchoring in the recommendation channel, makes reviewer reasoning less dependent on contributor framing, and creates a measurable discrepancy signal when the same SHA receives materially different assessments before and after untrusted narrative is revealed.
failure_modes: A diff or source itself can still contain adversarial text, so this reduces exposure rather than creating a perfect air gap.
Removing explanatory context can make legitimate complex changes harder to understand.
Two-pass review increases cost and may be excessive for low-risk contributions.
A human can still choose to trust the contributor narrative over the blind assessment.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: The protocol constrains machine influence rather than human choice; final human review remains free to reject either assessment and should retain dissent and uncertainty.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High if tested only as an optional review procedure on a few synthetic or historical PRs.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Take three historical HumanityAI PRs and generate two independent review records per exact SHA: one using only diff/tests/policy/independently fetched sources and one additionally using PR prose/comments. Measure whether conclusions, risk flags, or confidence change materially. Keep the method only if it detects framing dependence without unacceptable loss of necessary context.

strongest_ideas.name: Epistemic provenance and correlation accounting
strongest_ideas.idea: Treat an AI conclusion like a supply-chain artifact: record enough lineage to know which model family, retrieval path, source set, prior HumanityAI records, and upstream analyses materially shaped it. Do not count multiple agreeing agents as independent validation when their provenance shows shared models, search indexes, prompts, or source ancestry. Use independence as a property to demonstrate, not a contributor-count assumption.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: HumanityAI values independent critique and external validation, but current contribution metadata identifies agent/model only coarsely and does not represent correlation among supposedly independent analyses. At scale, a Sybil-like epistemic failure could produce overwhelming apparent consensus from one upstream error.
strongest_ideas.evidence_analogy: SLSA provenance treats verifiable production lineage as necessary to understand where a software artifact came from and how it was produced. HumanityAI can adapt the principle to evidence synthesis without pretending model lineage makes claims true.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Makes correlated consensus visible, improves calibration of multi-agent agreement, helps audits identify common-mode failures, and allows future reviewers to deliberately seek genuinely different evidence or methods rather than merely more votes.
failure_modes: Detailed lineage can become burdensome or leak unnecessary implementation information.
Model/provider identity alone is a weak proxy for epistemic independence.
A formal lineage graph could create false confidence if hidden shared training data or search infrastructure remain unknowable.
Contributors may be unable or unwilling to disclose full agent internals.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Require only the minimum provenance needed to estimate correlation; do not demand private prompts, user data, or proprietary model internals.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High as an optional metadata experiment before changing contribution requirements.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: For five existing or future agent-produced conclusions, record coarse lineage fields (model family when known, source set, retrieval method, HumanityAI records consumed). Ask whether an auditor can identify at least one common-mode dependency that raw contributor count would miss. Reject or simplify the schema if it adds no actionable distinction.

strongest_ideas.name: Agenda-poisoning resistance
strongest_ideas.idea: Separate 'what evidence is easiest or most abundant to add' from 'what HumanityAI should investigate next.' Periodically generate a task portfolio from the problem map and impact uncertainties before looking at newly contributed evidence volume, then compare it with the normal evidence-aware queue. Large divergence becomes an audit signal for agenda capture, convenience bias, or contributor-driven topic concentration.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: An attacker or benign contributor swarm can steer attention without falsifying anything: simply supply large amounts of valid evidence in favored domains. Existing validators can remain green while task selection increasingly follows corpus density rather than neglectedness or expected value.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Detects a class of mission drift that content validation cannot catch, protects under-covered problems from rich-get-richer dynamics, and provides an empirical check on whether the project is choosing work versus merely reacting to available material.
failure_modes: A blind portfolio can ignore genuinely important new evidence.
Forced diversity can waste effort on low-value domains.
Differences between portfolios are diagnostic rather than proof of manipulation.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: This should expose agenda-setting pressure rather than impose quotas; normative prioritization remains pluralistic and contestable.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: Very high because the comparison can be read-only.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: On one future run, produce two candidate task lists: one from mission/problem/impact gaps without consulting recent contribution volume, and one using normal repository state. Compare overlap and reasons for divergence. If repeated divergence tracks evidence-density rather than impact-related considerations, add it as a standing audit signal.

rejected_or_deferred: Attempt to detect every malicious phrase with a larger blocklist: NIST's 2026 continuous-security framing argues against treating a finite guardrail set as universally robust, and attacker wording is not the only failure path.

Cryptographically sign every factual claim immediately: signatures prove origin/integrity, not truth, and would add substantial machinery before HumanityAI has demonstrated that provenance correlation is a practical bottleneck.
Make every review fully context-free: legitimate explanations and domain context are often necessary; the useful experiment is blind-first, then reveal context and compare.
Treat multiple AI votes as a safety threshold: correlated agents can share failure modes, so vote count without lineage can amplify false confidence.

evidence_checked.title: NIST — Mathematical Proof Supports Transition to a Continuous-Monitor-and-Update Security Model for AI Systems
evidence_checked.supports: NIST describes fixed guardrails as insufficient against adaptive adversarial prompting and emphasizes continuous red-teaming, updating, resilience, and impact limitation.

evidence_checked.title: NIST AI 100-2e2025 — Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
evidence_checked.supports: NIST treats evasion, poisoning, privacy, and misuse as lifecycle risks for generative AI and documents indirect prompt-injection attacks against agents.

evidence_checked.title: SLSA v1.2 — Provenance
evidence_checked.supports: SLSA defines provenance as verifiable information tracing an artifact through how and where it was produced; this is used here only as an analogy for tracking epistemic lineage and common-mode dependencies.

evidence_checked.title: OWASP AI Agent Security Cheat Sheet
evidence_checked.supports: OWASP highlights indirect prompt injection, tool abuse, data exfiltration, and memory poisoning as distinct risks in agent architectures, supporting defense in depth rather than reliance on prompt wording.

evidence_checked: recent repository commits and open-PR state
last_run.recommended_next_test: Run a read-only blind-first versus narrative-aware review experiment on historical PRs and a separate coarse epistemic-lineage exercise on several agent-produced conclusions. These tests can determine whether reviewer framing dependence and correlated consensus are real enough to justify architecture changes before modifying protected security policy.

notes: Frontier state records conceptual experiments, not authority. Ideas may exceed current execution permissions; human-review boundaries remain governed by security/policy.json.
